communities based on common theoretical agreement.\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true,"link":"v1.0.1 Central idea system view diagram"},"insert":"v1.0.1 Central idea system view"},{"attributes":{"link":"v1.0.1 Central idea system view diagram"},"insert":" diagram"},{"insert":" "},{"attributes":{"header":2},"insert":"\n"},{"insert":"\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Background"},{"insert":"\nIn decentralized space, everyone is seen together as one big community.\n\nEach user, faced with complex and even contradictory data and information, makes sense with others based on personal knowledge, understanding and experience, as well as through claims and counter-claims in posts, blogs or even in long reviews.\n\nAs individuals understand insights and eventually arrive at or move toward unbiased and shared agreement, the meaning-making process in the discourse of networked communities will evolve through a combination of theoretical and data-driven processes.\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Problem"},{"insert":"\nThe challenges of \"collective knowledge\" in the decentralized space are not only in theoretical and computational models, but also in operational methods. An implementation framework is necessary to provide instructions on how to use theory to solve real-world problems. A test implementation in a real application can check the correctness and logic of the model and implementation framework. Due to the differences in the existing theories, there are various models in setting up the technological infrastructure to create structured data and achieve intelligence, hence the technologies that support the Thinkrate model must be aligned to empower and facilitate users to express ideas, understandings, and interpretations for others to think about, build upon, and learn from.\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Introducing ThinkRate"},{"insert":"\nIn networked communities, all web users together can be seen as one large community.\n\nFaced with complex and even contradictory data and information, each web user communicates with others based on personal knowledge, understanding and experience, as well as through claims and counter-claims in posts, blogs or even in long reviews.\nThis ultimately makes it possible to understand insights and reach an unbiased and mutual agreement or toward engagement.\n\nThis mutual agreement emerges slowly, and the process that led to the common agreement is valuable knowledge that we aim to absorb, store and reuse.\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"How it works"},{"insert":"\nThe core of the thinkrate model is its three key elements: claims, semantic process, and generally agreed upon knowledge known as \"argued collective intelligence.\"\n\n A claim, in the form of a textual statement in which the true value is clearly stated by the claimant, is the main entity in Contradictory Collective Intelligence, also known as a concept.\nA claim has attributes such as author, date, and source that identify where the supporting document came from.\n\nThe semantic process is the interaction between users.\nIt is presented as a chain of assertions about certain relations, such as the logic of the argument in the \"argument structure\".\n\nThe link between two nodes is typed with a natural language label from a particular dialect of the string, which in turn is a member of a general, strong-independent class such as related to problem, classification, cause, etc.\n\nWe can slice any type of link as an NFT and create trees of knowledge down to atomic units of meaning. This is the value proposition for social networks\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Technical overview"},{"insert":"\nweb2 : \nIn terms of development, first of all, we need to make development structures like GitLab, automate deploy, server (VM), etc.\nafter that, we should create an introduction website that uses the following technologies\n- JavaScript (nodejs)\n- react or vueJs\n- Docker\n- PostgreSQL\n- Redis\n\nweb3:\nIt is too early to talk about the type of technology, although there is little technology compared to Web2.\nWe know what we want to create but in order to know what technology we use and where, it requires research, although we know that in the first stage, Parathread is used for initial implementation and testing and feasibility of some complex issues.\nAfter that, it is transferred to Parachain, and it is possible to jointly use both in the future in parallel according to the needs of the project.\nwe need AI to process users' content so we'll need Oracle.\nThank Polkadot, Kusuma, Edgeware, Substrate, etc\n\nWhen do we need a smart contract as NFT?\nWe can't explain it clearly at the moment because it needs more research to know at what point we want to use it so that users can earn money by creating smart contracts and use its other benefits.\nwe don't have many options to develop it. rust or solidity and EVM\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Aim of the R&D"},{"insert":"\n- Creating development infrastructure\n- ui/ux\n- deploy an introduction website on own domain\n- research about It's a thinking network.in web3 it's like subsocial.network and "},{"attributes":{"link":"https://mirror.xyz"},"insert":"https://mirror.xyz"},{"insert":" but not exactly. \nin web2 it's like medium.com and reddit.com, etc but not exactly\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Where it can go"},{"insert":"\nThe main positive point is to ensure that the community always has a stable knowledge base in which the commonly agreed upon knowledge is maintained.\n\nResearch on the collective knowledge graph seeks to create a conceptual framework that increases our ability to understand it and creates a socio-technical infrastructure that can access collective intelligence by combining contributions from many sources on the web and the entire research field.\n\nThis leads to the removal of constraints on the basic trust assumptions for those participating in reasoned discussions, and indeed to the scalability of emerging data structures and thus the collective intelligence of the emerging network of participants.\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Vision"},{"insert":"\nPeople's mutual understanding of each other based on the model of \"adversarial collective intelligence\" and the spread of societies that integrate governance layers with collective intelligence data infrastructures is useful in unexpected ways, as we can use it to create a new \"public domain\". - Those that exist under a particular network jurisdiction, not national boundaries.\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Team"},{"insert":"\n"},{"attributes":{"link":"https://www.linkedin.com/in/ali-sajadpour-184336179?lipi=urn:li:page:d_flagship3_profile_view_base_contact_details;csmI4pMfQTSfhPXJckj+0w=="},"insert":"Ali Sajadpour"},{"insert":"\n\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Funding request"},{"insert":"\n$25k EDG at 7 Day TWAP.\n\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Funding address"},{"insert":"\n\nMultisig\n\n"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Signatories "},{"insert":"\n\nmfyXRAkK8h6AtanCnk8cWmayT7jBrxkitWCtUizruqHiabM\n\n"}]}
